opportunities.title: No published LLM benchmark results
opportunities.detail: Neither of the two multilingual benchmarks we track reports this language. Adding it would give builders and buyers a baseline.
opportunities.why: About 2.4 million Kinyarwanda speakers are online and able to text today, and that should reach 3.4 million within five years. Ready to use: FLORES-200 (covers this language); Belebele (covers this language).

opportunities.title: No cloud text-to-speech voice found, though open resources exist
opportunities.detail: None of the cloud services checked has a voice for this language. An open text-to-speech model already speaks it. Open datasets hold 2,016 hours of transcribed speech.
opportunities.why: About 3.1 million Kinyarwanda speakers are online today, and that should reach 4.4 million within five years. Ready to use: MMS text-to-speech (covers this language); YODAS2 (14 hours of transcribed speech).

opportunities.title: No published speech recognition error rate
opportunities.detail: The language isn't in the published FLEURS error-rate breakdowns we track, so builders can't tell how usable open speech recognition is.
opportunities.why: About 3.1 million Kinyarwanda speakers are online today, and that should reach 4.4 million within five years. Ready to use: YODAS2 (14 hours of transcribed speech); Mozilla Common Voice (2,002 hours of transcribed speech).

opportunities.title: The interface is translated on 1 of 3 major platforms
opportunities.detail: People can already use some phone and computer platforms in this language. Shared terminology would make the remaining ones faster to translate.
opportunities.why: About 2.4 million Kinyarwanda speakers are online and able to text today, and that should reach 3.4 million within five years. Ready to use: Unicode CLDR (basic coverage).

opportunities.title: Speech input is offered by 2 of 4 major services
opportunities.detail: Some services already recognise this language. Open training data includes 2,016 hours of transcribed speech across 2 open datasets.
opportunities.why: About 3.1 million Kinyarwanda speakers are online today, and that should reach 4.4 million within five years. Ready to use: YODAS2 (14 hours of transcribed speech); Mozilla Common Voice (2,002 hours of transcribed speech).

opportunities.title: No text recognition, open or commercial
opportunities.detail: Printed books, signs and forms can't be read by phone cameras or digitised at scale.
opportunities.why: About 2.4 million Kinyarwanda speakers are online and able to text today, and that should reach 3.4 million within five years.

opportunities.title: Locale data in Unicode CLDR is basic
opportunities.detail: Complete CLDR data (names, dates, numbers, character sets) underpins interface localisation, keyboards and reading numbers aloud in text-to-speech.
opportunities.why: About 2.4 million Kinyarwanda speakers are online and able to text today, and that should reach 3.4 million within five years. Ready to use: Unicode CLDR (basic coverage).

opportunities.title: Predictive text and autocorrect could be built from open text
opportunities.detail: The iOS keyboard has 0 of 4 typing features. FineWeb-2 holds about 128 million words of openly licensed web text, enough to train word prediction.
opportunities.why: About 2.4 million Kinyarwanda speakers are online and able to text today, and that should reach 3.4 million within five years. Ready to use: FineWeb-2 (128 million words); Wikipedia (11 thousand articles).

opportunities.title: Translation is offered by 2 of 3 major services
opportunities.detail: An open model and the FLORES-200 evaluation set already cover this language, so the main remaining step is a product launch.
opportunities.why: About 2.4 million Kinyarwanda speakers are online and able to text today, and that should reach 3.4 million within five years. Ready to use: NLLB-200 (covers this language); FLORES-200 (covers this language).

opportunities.title: Wikipedia has 67 active editors
opportunities.detail: A small editing community limits new open text. Edit-a-thons and translation drives with universities have grown communities elsewhere.
